name: rsdmx
what_it_holds: R package/client for reading SDMX-ML and SDMX-JSON data and metadata from any SDMX-compliant provider (Eurostat, OECD, IMF, ILO, UNSD, and many national statistical/tourism offices that publish via SDMX). Not a dataset itself; a generic connector. 110 stars, actively used, GPL-ish/open license, maintained multi-year.
why_useful: Lets us systematically pull monthly tourism arrivals/nights/receipts and accommodation-capacity series from dozens of national statistics agencies (gap #7 LatAm/APAC volume, gap #4 point-in-time vintages if the provider keeps dataflow versions) instead of one country at a time.
time_coverage: varies by provider, typically monthly, multi-year
size_hint: connector library, not a fixed dataset
themes: wildcard: a national tourism-statistics official who knows which agenc
why_all: Lets us systematically pull monthly tourism arrivals/nights/receipts and accommodation-capacity series from dozens of national statistics agencies (gap #7 LatAm/APAC volume, gap #4 point-in-time vintages if the provider keeps dataflow versions) instead of one country at a time.

name: Data-Pipeline-for-analyzing-Inside-Airbnb-dataset

name: inside-airbnb-tutorial
category_note: academic/teaching tooling for pulling Inside Airbnb data on a schedule
what_it_holds: Tilburg Science Hub tutorial/pipeline for pulling Inside Airbnb's monthly-updated calendar.csv and listings.csv programmatically (documented ETL steps rather than a one-off notebook).
why_useful: A maintained, documented pull method (vs. ad hoc scripts) for Inside Airbnb calendar/listings data that could be adapted into our own point-in-time capture pipeline to get monthly vintages before the CDN drops them (addresses part of gap #1's forward-looking side: capturing dumps before they age off).
themes: Airbnb calendar / availability / blocked-night datasets and occupancy-estimation code (San Francisco model, review-to-booking ratios)
